gloss: three mon (old coin); a pittance; cheap

definitions.gloss: three mon (old copper coin unit); a pittance; trifling amount
definitions.explanation: Literally 'three mon' — three units of an old copper coin worth almost nothing. Now used figuratively in idioms to mean 'a trifle', 'a cheap thing', or 'a small but real benefit'.

examples.japanese: ⟦{早起|はやお}き→早起き：02477_hayaoki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三文|さんもん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{得|とく}→得：12563_toku⟧。
examples.english: The early bird catches the worm. (lit. 'rising early is worth three mon')

examples.japanese: ⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三文|さんもん}⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すぎない。
examples.english: That's nothing more than a cheap pulp novel.

examples.japanese: {三文|さんもん}⟦{役者|やくしゃ}→役者：05113_yakusha⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれて→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}ち→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧た。
examples.english: Even though he was called a third-rate actor, he kept performing on stage every day.

notes:
⟦{文|もん}→文：29590_mon⟧ was a unit of old Japanese copper coinage; three of them was a very small sum. In modern Japanese the word survives almost exclusively in fixed phrases meaning 'cheap' or 'trifling'.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{早起|はやお}き→早起き：02477_hayaoki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三文|さんもん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{得|とく}→得：12563_toku⟧: 'rising early is worth three mon' — the early bird gets a small benefit
- {三文|さんもん}⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧: pulp novel; trashy fiction
- {三文|さんもん}⟦{役者|やくしゃ}→役者：05113_yakusha⟧: third-rate / hack actor
- {三文|さんもん}{文士|ぶんし}: hack writer
- {二束|にそく}{三文|さんもん}: dirt cheap (two bundles for three mon)

USAGE:
Rarely used as a literal price in modern Japanese — almost always appears as part of an idiom or set expression with a 'cheap, worthless, or trivial' nuance.
